DOBARA

Game design document

    Game design document · NID Design Project 02

    DOBARAदोबारा · "again" · the one who comes back

    Bengaluru, 2038. A con artist walks out of prison with a cracked brass watch that can bend time, and goes after the man who shot his partner. Arkham City with a watch instead of gadgets.

    GenreThird-person stealth-action with time powers
    PlatformPC, keyboard and mouse or gamepad
    EngineUnity 6 (6000.4), URP, Input System
    TeamSanidhya Dev Gupta, solo
    Vertical sliceMission 12, "The Man Who Shot Her", about 17 minutes
    Full game (planned)A prologue, 18 missions in 8 acts, an epilogue
    Submission14 November 2026
    Documentv0.1, 22 October 2026, built from the narrative, the design notes and the Unity project
    Section 01

    Vision

    Pitch

    Rehaan was raised at a watchmaker's bench in old Bengaluru and grew up into a con artist who plans everything. In 2028 he stole his mentor's brass watch for one last con, and watched his partner Meher shot dead across a card table. He pressed the crown to undo it, and the watch cracked against a moment that would not change. Ten years later he walks out of prison, the watchmaker repairs the watch, and Rehaan starts taking apart the network that framed him. The street starts calling him Dobara: the one who keeps coming back.

    Every special verb in the game comes from the Watch. It has four powers, and each one acts on exactly one kind of thing: Possibility reads the placeRewind restores one objectSlow acts on the worldFast Forward acts on Rehaan

    The Watch lets him change moments. The story teaches him when not to change a life.

    Design pillars

    1. Plan with time. Read the level, then spend a limited Charge on a chain of powers that opens it. A plan has to fit inside the Watch.
    2. One power, one target. Each power works on one kind of thing, so a player can look at any object and know which power it needs.
    3. The planner who has to jump. Stealth is the planned path; the fight is what happens when the plan breaks. The game's structure is Rehaan's flaw.
    4. Bengaluru as a character. Sodium-lit old city against cold glass city, tanker yards, water crisis, camera grids. The environment carries the story.
    5. Nobody dies until the abyss. Takedowns knock men out. There is one killing in the game, and the player presses it.

    The brief

    NID Design Project 02: a narrative-based 3D superhero game in an Indian context. Themes to hit: the hero's journey, light and darkness, power and responsibility, the Indian context, visual storytelling, the environment as a storytelling tool, and the contrast between hero and nemesis. Deliverables: this GDD, a playable vertical slice, a gameplay video and an A3 poster.

    Players

    Players who like third-person stealth-action and readable melee: the Batman Arkham games for the predator stealth and freeflow fights, Sifu for close-quarters combat with clear wind-ups. The time powers add a puzzle layer on top for players who like planning a route before they take it.

    Design thinking

    What kind of superhero belongs in Bengaluru?

    Problem
    The brief asked for a superhero game in an Indian context. Imported superhero tropes (capes, origin-by-accident, saving the city from aliens) don't sit in a real Indian city, and the hero needed a mechanic that is also his character.
    Alternatives
    A gravity-shifting hero; a Chronicle-style group of friends with powers; a mythology-based hero. Mythology as a mechanic was ruled out: it pulls the game away from a grounded city.
    Decided by
    A grounded story with one fantastical element: a watch. A watchmaker's apprentice turned con artist makes the powers personal. He understands mechanisms, believes every failure has a cause, and thinks enough planning prevents loss. The Watch tests exactly that belief.
    Result
    The first DOBARA draft (revenge, a rewind watch, Bengaluru) grew into the current version: four powers with strict rules, three targets in arcs, and an antagonist who set up both sides of the con to prove that anyone given power will choose themselves.
    Section 02

    Story and world

    The story in short

    2013. Nine-year-old Rehaan tries to steal from Narayan Achar's watch shop in Shivajinagar. Narayan sits him on a stool and opens the watch instead: "You wanted this? Then learn what it is." A year later Meher arrives, a girl from two lanes over who jumps from rooftops Rehaan is still measuring. At twelve, Rehaan sees Narayan un-break a glass of chai with a brass watch he keeps in a locked drawer.

    2028. Rehaan and Meher run small cons. Meher wants a house by the sea. An anonymous buyer, the crime boss Suresh Nayak, will pay a fortune for "the Achar piece". Rehaan takes the real Watch from Narayan's drawer to show at the table. The same week the same intermediary warns Nayak that the sellers are con artists. At the door Meher turns back and says something sharp. Nayak shoots her. Rehaan presses the crown; the Watch splits the next second into ghost-futures, strains against something that will not move, and cracks. Her death is a fixed point.

    2038. Framed by the broker Shalini Rai, Rehaan serves ten years. He refuses every one of Narayan's visits and opens none of his letters. Released, he goes back to the shop. Narayan repairs the Watch without a word about the drawer and opens the basement under the shop. Rehaan pins Meher's photo and Nayak's to the wall, and works up the chain: Rai, who wrote the case; Vikram Kothari, who built violet copies of the Watch from a scan of it; and Nayak.

    The abyss. At the end of the Nayak arc Rehaan beats him, and Nayak laughs: he was told they were coming. He shows the unsigned warning, marked with an off-centre dot. Rehaan shoots him with the gun that killed Meher. On a water tower above the yard, Dr. Aniruddh Sen, Narayan's old research partner, closes his notebook. He has his result.

    Dobara. The city erupts. Narayan can barely look at Rehaan. Sen, the Observer, offers him a branch of time where Meher lives. Meher, in the branch, says what she always said: "You can't plan everything. Sometimes you just have to jump." Rehaan walks back to his own timeline. Narayan seals the branching for good, Meher's photo goes into a drawer, and a new case goes up on the board.

    Bengaluru, 2038–39

    Glass city against old city. Automation layoffs emptied the tech parks in the early 2030s. A water crisis in 2033 put the tankers in Nayak's hands. In 2034 Rai sold the city a camera grid, and in 2038 security marks what it sees: camera domes throw a red laser grid over exactly the ground they watch. Online betting went underground.

    Districts

    • Old City: Shivajinagar, KR Market, Chickpet. Achar Watch Works.
    • Commercial: MG Road, the emptied Outer Ring Road tech parks.
    • Industrial: Peenya, tanker yards, Kothari's hardware.
    • Entertainment: Frazer Town gambling dens, rooftop clubs.
    • Administrative: the Cubbon Park area, the old university lab.
    • Underground: storm drains, metro tunnels.

    The events of the 2030s are invented. Real-world details (the online gaming ban, the city's split governance) are to be checked before the jury.

    Design thinking

    How do you make "power and responsibility" a choice, not a lecture?

    Problem
    A revenge story usually rewards the revenge. The brief asked for power and responsibility, and the story's whole point is that Rehaan's need to control things is what got Meher killed.
    Decided by
    The player is never given a choice at the abyss: one prompt, the shot, silence. The game makes the player complicit, then spends its last acts on the cost. The real choice comes in the finale, where the branch with Meher alive is offered and the player walks Rehaan back out of it.
    Result
    The rules of the Watch carry the theme: fixed points hold, it never changes a person, and the one power that acts on the wearer, Fast Forward, is the one Narayan doesn't trust. "It makes a man faster than his own judgement."
    Section 03

    The Watch

    The object

    Brass, 40 mm, a cream dial with no numerals. The 2028 crack is kept under a new crystal. Four power inlays sit at 12, 3, 6 and 9: silver, amber, deep blue and copper. Narayan sets the fourth, copper, the night before the slice. Rehaan wears it over his sleeve, with Meher's red thread beside it.

    Rules

    • Local only. Every power works on something near Rehaan.
    • Never a person. It never changes a person; the wearer is the only exception.
    • Fixed points hold. Some moments can't be undone. Some objects, put back where they belong, lock and stay.

    Charge

    The Watch runs on 100 Charge, refilling at 5 per second out of combat. In a fight it refills only from landed hits (about 3 each). A level's main route costs roughly 85–110 Charge, with time to regain some between steps. Optional routes cost extra.

    The four powers (current tuning)
    PowerKey / padActs onCostWhat it does
    PossibilityQ / LBReads the placefree, regen pausedDetective mode. The world drops to black with blue-grey edges. Guards burn red through walls; calm guards show their routes with silver afterimages walking them ahead of time. Rewindable objects replay their history in amber. Things Rehaan could use glow in the colour of the power they need. His own possible paths walk ahead of him as orange ghosts; a blue ghost shows a takedown when he's behind a guard.
    RewindE / RB
    while aiming    		One object25Aim at one object within 15 m and hold: it runs back along its last 8 seconds at double speed. Let go and it carries on with that moment's momentum. Objects with a fixed point lock in place when rewound into it.
    SlowR / RTThe world round a point30A 6 m dome of quarter-speed time for 4 s, where he aims (up to 20 m) or around himself. Machines, cameras, timers and men crawl inside it. Never Rehaan. One dome at a time.
    Fast ForwardF / R3Rehaan only30A 5 s burst at double movement and animation speed with a copper streak. In a fight, a burst is freeflow (section 07).
    Design thinking

    Why does each power act on only one kind of thing?

    Problem
    In the first power set, Fast Forward did two jobs: it hurried Rehaan and it could also advance a machine's process up to 60 s ahead, overlapping with Slow and Rewind on the same objects. Possibility only desaturated the screen, so it showed little.
    Decided by
    Strict roles: Possibility reads, Rewind restores one object, Slow acts on the world round the reticle, Fast Forward acts on Rehaan only. Process-advancing was dropped. Possibility became a full detective mode. Every level then needs a chain that uses each power in a taught order.
    After play
    Aiming, Rewind, Slow, Possibility's trails and rewind frames, and Fast Forward in the pump house were play-tested in the greybox. The outflow room still needs tuning.
    Section 04

    Core loops and flows

    Level structure rule

    Each level has one main chain that needs every power the player has, in the order the level teaches it, and one or two optional routes that reuse the powers differently and include a takedown. The target for a main route is about 85–110 Charge; as built, the tanker yard's costs about 105–115 and the pump house's about 110, spread across steps so the Charge refills in between. Optional routes cost extra, so taking one is a trade.

    Section 05

    Controls

    One layout, two modes (explore / combat)
    Verb (explore / combat)GamepadKeyboard and mouse
    Move / lookLeft stick / right stickWASD / mouse
    Aim (hold)LTRight mouse in explore, Ctrl in combat
    Takedown / strikeXLeft mouse
    Interact / counterYG / right mouse
    Climb / evadeASpace
    Crouch / stunBC
    Sprint (hold)L3Shift
    Possibility · Rewind (while aiming) · Slow · Fast ForwardLB · RB · RT · R3Q · E · R · F
    PauseStartEsc

    Movement and camera

    • Walk 1.65 m/s, sprint 5.25 (hold), crouch 1.19 (toggle). Crouching cuts guards' sight range to 0.6× and halves how fast they grow suspicious.
    • Orbit camera with Rehaan left of centre; it pulls in when walls get between.
    • Aim (hold): over the shoulder, lower sensitivity, Rehaan faces the aim and strafes, no sprint. The shared reticle shows only while aiming.
    • Cover: walk into a wall for 0.15 s to take low or high cover. Slide along it, peek past edges, aim to pop out, push away to leave. Props and guards aren't cover.
    • Vents: in a duct the camera switches to first person, then hands back facing the same way.

    Why this layout

    Each button is the nearest verb in both modes, so muscle memory carries from stealth into the first fight: the takedown button is the strike, the interact button is the counter, climb is evade, crouch is stun. Nothing used under pressure is on the d-pad.

    The four powers sit on the shoulders and R3 in the order the story gives them, and Rewind only fires while aiming, so it never goes off by accident.

    Takedowns and grabs

    Takedowns knock men out; nobody dies. From behind and outside the guard's cone, within 1.6 m: a chokehold (about 3.8 s, Rehaan held in the animation). From the front, only on a guard who has turned toward a noise rather than something he saw: a single strike. A guard who is already alerted can't be taken down. A knocked-out guard stays down where he fell.

    A guard who reaches Rehaan grabs him: he lunges, holds him for 1.5 s, and the beat restarts at the checkpoint with 75% Charge. Stealth beats have no combat at all, so being seen is never a way into a fight.

    Security cameras

    A camera's head sweeps back and forth at 30°/s, pausing 1 s at each end. It watches a narrow wedge (±15°), and in 2038 security marks what it sees: a red laser grid draped over exactly that ground, calm and steady, brighter and flickering as its meter fills, strobing on alarm. A full meter calls every guard within 20 m to the spot. Every power has an answer: Slow slows the sweep, Rewind scrubs the head back along its arc (it keeps watching), and Fast Forward through the cone halves how fast the meter fills.

    Design thinking

    How does a player see what a camera sees?

    Problem
    A security camera's detection area is invisible, so getting spotted by one feels unfair, and a cone that's bigger or smaller than it looks makes timing guesswork.
    Decided by
    An answer inside the world that fits 2038: cameras throw a red laser grid over exactly the ground they detect. It drapes over props and over Rehaan, and its brightness shows the meter, so players read the danger in the world rather than on the HUD. The story uses it too: in M1 every junction's camera lays its grid on the wet road.
    Result
    The laser grid is built and drawing in the greybox. How it looks is still to be checked in play.
    Section 07

    Combat

    Freeflow is Fast Forward

    Rehaan has never fought in his life. Outside a burst he fights small and close: strikes only reach 2.6 m, and he can counter and evade. Press Fast Forward and the 5 s burst is freeflow: he closes gaps of up to 12 m between blows, moves at double speed and hits 1.5× harder. The fight's rhythm is the Charge: hits refill it (+3 each), bursts spend it.

    The Watch reads the fight

    A passive Possibility runs in every fight, free. An enemy winds up for about 0.6 s. If he's the only attacker and the hit can be countered, his red afterimage plays the blow a moment early: that's the counter window. If two blows will land within 0.4 s, or the attack can't be countered (the knife, the brute's charge), Rehaan's own orange afterimage shows where to dodge. Pressing Possibility mid-fight reads the threat: who attacks next, the knife, the brute's charge line.

    Verbs
    VerbInputEffect
    StrikeX / left mouse10 damage, +1 combo, +3 Charge. Picks the enemy most in line with the stick. Presses chain.
    CounterY / right mouseOnly in the red cue's window: staggers him, lands a blow, Rehaan untouchable for the move. A miss locks him out for 0.35 s.
    EvadeA / Space2.6 m dodge, untouchable for the whole dodge, keeps the combo, cancels hit-stun.
    StunB / CDazes one enemy for about 1.5 s and interrupts a wind-up. The brute must be stunned to be hittable. No combo.
    Ground finishStrike on a downed enemyA stomp that knocks him out for good.
    Finisherbanked every 10 comboKnocks out one enemy, Rehaan untouchable during it. Stacks. Not on bosses.

    Health and knockdowns

    • Rehaan takes about six hits (60 health, 10 per hit), regenerates out of combat after 4 s. At zero: fade, restart the fight's checkpoint at 75% Charge.
    • Brawlers have 40 health. Any hit that leaves one standing has a 10% chance (20% in Fast Forward) to knock him down. On the ground, a ground finish knocks him out; otherwise he gets up after 3 s and can go down again.
    • Combo resets when Rehaan is hit or after 2.5 s without a hit.
    • Slow in a fight: enemies and their cues run at quarter speed (bigger windows) and slowed hits do half damage.
    Enemies in the slice
    EnemyAnswer
    Armed guardStealth only: sight, hearing, grabs. Shooting deferred.
    BrawlerCounter his red cue; knock down, ground finish.
    KnifeCan't be countered: dodge, or Rewind disarms him.
    BruteCharges and grabs: Slow him, stun to make him hittable.
    Suresh NayakThree phases (section 08).
    Design thinking

    Why is freeflow tied to Fast Forward?

    Problem
    The plan began as Sifu-style close-quarters combat. But Rehaan is a planner who has never fought, and the slice's story beat is the moment he stops planning. If he fights like a trained hero from the first punch, the "jump" means nothing.
    Decided by
    Decided on 22 October: outside a burst he fights small and close; Fast Forward, the power that acts on him alone, makes him fast enough to fight a room. The power Narayan distrusts is the one that turns him into a fighter.
    After play
    The first play-test changed three things the same day: freeflow is gated by Fast Forward (2.6 m reach outside, 12 m inside), a fixed knockdown at half health became a random 10% / 20% chance per hit, and the ground finish moved onto the strike button. The evade now cancels hit-stun and is untouchable for the whole dodge.
    Section 08

    Vertical slice: M12

    The Man Who Shot Her

    Nayak's tanker-yard compound in Peenya, where the city's water trucks fill at night: sodium lamps in winter haze, tankers in rows, men on the gantries. About 17 minutes, covering stealth, a puzzle, the first fight, a boss and the abyss. Four spaces only: the basement, the tanker yard, the pump house and the tanker bay. Characters: Rehaan, Narayan, Nayak, one crew body (guard, brawler, knife, brute), Sen as a silhouette, Meher in stills.

    1 · The basement

    cold open · cutscene · 1.5 min

    Winter haze. The board: Nayak's photo at the centre, strings running to it from everything else. Narayan comes down the stairs and puts the Watch on the bench with the fourth inlay set, copper beside the brass.

    "This one acts on you. Nobody else. It doesn't wait for you to be ready. Only if you have to."
    "I've planned for everything."

    2 · The tanker yard

    stealth · 4 min · built

    Three rows of water tankers under seven sodium lamps; the lanes between them are the dark ground. An inner fence crosses the north with a gantry walkway behind it, and the crane stands in the north-east bay. Rehaan enters at the south-west gate and leaves by the stair house in the north-west corner.

    Main chain (map numbers)

    1. Gate camera. Its red grid sweeps the only lane in. SLOW its sweep, or REWIND the head back along its arc, and walk the gap past the gate guard.
    2. South lane. A guard patrols east–west across the whole yard. Choke him from behind, or wait for his back.
    3. Crane load. It lies dropped in the gap in the inner fence. REWIND it back up onto its hook: the gap opens.
    4. The swing. Hooked, the load swings across the gap (4 m rope, ±50°, 4 s). FAST FORWARD through it, or SLOW it and walk under. A camera on the fence watches the gap.
    5. Decoy crates. They fell silently before he arrived. REWIND them so they fall again, loud (heard at 14 m): both gantry guards walk east to look.
    6. Stair house. Walk in and go down to the pump house.

    Optional: the west dark route hugs the west wall north, then cuts east along the north lane. The gantry high route climbs the east stairs from the crane gap (+4 m) and walks the gantry west, with a takedown on one of its two guards.

    • Size 70 × 50 m
    • Guards 6
    • Cameras 2
    • Main route ~105–115 Charge
    PieceDetail
    GuardsGate, south lane, north lane, gantry west and east (+4 m), crane bay loop
    CamerasGate cam: 70° sweep, 12 m. Fence cam on the crane gap: 60°, 10 m
    RewindCrane load (socket on the hook), 3 decoy crates, 2 loose crates by the gate

    3 · The pump house

    puzzle · 3 min · built

    Underground and L-shaped. The gallery and hall run along the south; the junction leg runs north up the east side to a button door; beyond it the outflow room opens to the north, with a mezzanine and the exit to the tanker bay.

    Main chain (map numbers)

    1. Start, at the foot of the stairs from the yard.
    2. Start shutter. It slams shut in front of him. REWIND it up: at the top its gear housing tears out of the wall, flies across the gallery, and the shutter drops again.
    3. Gear housing. REWIND it back into the wall. It seats in its socket and locks (a fixed point), and the shutter opens for good.
    4. Hall. One guard works the pump floor east–west. Take him from behind.
    5. Button A, under the junction camera. Press it, then SLOW it so it stays in for about 4.5 s instead of 1.5 s.
    6. Button B, about 33 m north. FAST FORWARD up the junction leg past the patrol while A is still in.
    7. Button door. With both buttons in at once, it opens for good.
    8. Outflow room. Climb the west-wall stairs to the mezzanine (+3.5 m) past the stair guard and the door guard.
    9. Upper exit door, under the door camera, into the tanker bay.

    Optional: the vent route runs from the hall through vent A into the fan room (first person, crouched): SLOW the big fan, step between its blades, and leave by vent B to the junction. The high route climbs to the catwalk (+3 m), takes down the catwalk guard, REWINDS the fallen gangway onto its ledge and comes down the ledge stairs to the junction.

    Beats 4 to 8 play out in one walled compound, as one continuous walk: the loading bay in the south for the trap and the first fight, a roller door in the dividing wall, and the tanker bay in the north for Nayak. Rehaan walks out through the east vehicle gate, under a water tower outside the north-east corner.

    Main chain (map numbers)

    1. The upper door from the pump house (+3.5 m) onto a walkway along the south wall.
    2. Foot of the stairs: the trap.
    3. The first fight, wave 1.
    4. Wave 2: the brute through the roller door, the knife from behind.
    5. The roller door stays open into the tanker bay.
    6. Nayak, phase 1.

    Decided 22 Oct

    • Nayak is only a voice on the speakers during the trap and the first fight. He's first seen when the roller door opens.
    • He works the hoses from the gantry in phase 2 while the fight stays on the floor.
    • Two valve wheels, one each side of the floor.

    4 · The trap

    scripted · 1 min

    At the foot of the walkway stairs the four floodlight towers snap on. Nayak's voice over the speakers: "Ten years and you still walk in the front door." He knew Rehaan was coming, exactly as he knew in 2028. Men come in through the west and east doors. For eleven missions, this meant start again.

    5 · The jump

    first fight · 3 min

    Memory: daylight, a rooftop, Meher already in the air, laughing back at him. "You can't plan everything. Sometimes you just have to jump." The copper inlay lights. The player presses F, and this time there is no plan to spend it on.

    The fight teaches the cues on the open floor between the floodlights, with only low cover and a parked trailer at the edges.

    • Wave 1: four brawlers, two from each side door.
    • Wave 2: the roller door lifts for the brute (SLOW him, stun him to make him hittable), and a knife man comes down the walkway stairs behind Rehaan: no counter, dodge only.

    6 · Nayak

    boss · 3 min · tanker bay
    PhaseNayakAnswer
    1Fights with two of his crew on the open floor in front of the filling bays.The freeflow verbs.
    2Alone: charges east–west down the lane between the parked tankers, and turns the high-pressure hoses on Rehaan from the gantry.SLOW the charge. REWIND a valve wheel open (one each side of the floor) so its hose bursts on him and throws him down.
    3Falls back towards the filling bays and draws the pistol, the same one.POSSIBILITY shows the ghost of the shot; REWIND tears the gun from his hand.

    What Rehaan could not do that night, he does now. The boss reuses the combat cues in scripted phases.

    7 · The abyss · 8 · The watcher

    1 min · 0.5 min

    Nayak on the wet concrete, laughing. "You think I chose you? I was told you were coming." He pulls out a creased, unsigned note marked with an off-centre dot. "Someone handed you to me. I just pulled the trigger."

    Rehaan is holding the gun that killed her. One prompt. No other option. The shot. Silence. The warm sodium light drains out of the frame.

    He walks out into the haze, the note in his fist. The camera rises to the top of a water tower, where a grey-coated old man writes one line in a notebook, closes it and walks away. Rehaan never looks up. End card: the dot.

    Design thinking

    Why does the slice end with the hero losing?

    Problem
    A vertical slice has to show the whole game in 17 minutes: stealth, puzzles, combat and the story's stakes. The obvious slice is the first mission, but at M1 Rehaan has one power and no fight.
    Alternatives
    An earlier draft, "The Achar Piece", condensed M1 and M4: release, the shop, the room, a warehouse, a fight and the board, ending on a question.
    Decided by
    M12: the first mission with all four powers. It introduces combat as a story beat, has a boss, and holds the game's turn. It shows the theme through play: a perfect plan, the plan collapsing, the jump, then a victory that is a moral loss.
    Result
    Scope stays tight: four spaces, one crew body reused for every enemy type, Meher only in stills. Nothing outside M12 (no exo-heavies, no violet tech, no Temporal Divergence).
    Section 09

    Art direction

    Stylised realism, hard noir shadows

    • The light rule: the old city is warm (sodium), the glass city is cold (LED), and daylight appears only in memories.
    • Weather by act: monsoon (acts I–III), winter haze (IV–VI), summer heat (VII–VIII). The slice is in winter haze.
    • Power colours: Possibility silver, Rewind amber, Slow deep blue, Fast Forward copper. Kothari's stolen tech is always violet.
    • Factions: Nayak's crew gold on white; Rai's people cyan and blend in; Kothari's hazard yellow and violet; the chaos factions orange, carrying Sen's off-centre dot.
    • The abyss: a grade drains the warm saturation to grey.

    Section 10

    UI and feedback

    What the player sees
    ElementBehaviour
    ReticleOnly while aiming. Amber over something Rewind can take, deep blue where Slow can land, white otherwise.
    Detection metersOver guards who are noticing Rehaan: white → yellow → red, with ? and !. Pointers at the screen edge for guards off-screen.
    Camera gridsIn the world, not the HUD: steady, brighter with a flicker as the meter fills, strobing on alarm. A dim red spot under the camera.
    Interact prompt"Press G / Y" on the nearest usable thing within 1.8 m and 80° of his facing.
    PossibilityFades in over 0.25 s: black with blue-grey edges and a vignette; everything usable tinted by the power it needs; exits green.
    HealthA bar at the bottom left, only in combat or when hurt.
    Combo×N, a bar to the next finisher, and pips for banked finishers.
    Takedown promptOn screen when a takedown is possible; in Possibility a blue ghost previews it.
    Section 11

    Technical design

    Stack and rules

    • Unity 6 (6000.4), URP, the new Input System, Cinemachine 3. Possibility's look is a full-screen edge pass on the renderer.
    • One owner per system. Charge lives only in the Watch controller, input only in the input router, flow only in the game-flow manager. Nothing is duplicated.
    • No magic numbers. Every gameplay value lives in one tuning asset, so play-tests change data, not code.
    • Never touch the global time scale. Slow scales animators, rigidbodies and objects' own clocks; Fast Forward only scales Rehaan.
    • Every system has a debug readout, all toggled together with F1.
    Systems
    SystemHow it works
    Game flowBeats load additively into a Bootstrap scene. Each beat sets the checkpoint, input mode, combat and whether Fast Forward is unlocked. A grab or defeat fades, reloads and restarts at the checkpoint with 75% Charge.
    RewindAn 8 s ring buffer per object, recorded each physics step (resting steps skipped). Fixed points: an object thrown from its socket at load treats that flight as its history; rewound within 0.35 m of the socket, it locks.
    SlowA dome that scales animator speed and rigidbody velocity and gravity; machines with their own clocks implement a time-scale interface.
    PossibilityGuards drawn through walls; route ghosts sampled from patrol paths; Rehaan's path ghosts walk the level's authored main and alternative paths at 2.5× walk speed.
    Stealth AINavMesh guards with a vision cone, suspicion meter and hearing. Light comes only from tagged stealth lights.
    CombatHealth and damage rules in one place; a director orders attackers; cue ghosts are posed from the attack clips themselves.
    LevelsLaid out in a web planner, exported as JSON and built by an editor importer that places prefabs, the spawn and exit, and rebakes navigation.
    Test labA hub with labelled pads and ten sealed bays, one per mechanic, each with a reset pad. Every new mechanic gets a bay.

    Built

    • Player: movement, crouch, cover, aim, first person in vents
    • All four powers, Charge and the aiming reticle
    • Stealth AI, hearing, light, detection HUD, security cameras and laser grids
    • Takedowns, grabs and checkpoint restarts
    • Combat: health, strikes, combo, counter and dodge cues, evade, knockdowns, ground finish
    • Levels: the tanker yard and the pump house greyboxed; the test lab

    Still to build

    • Stun, finishers, the knife and the brute, Nayak's three phases
    • The basement, the tanker bay, the board and evidence cards
    • Cutscenes: cold open, trap, memory, abyss, water tower
    • Climbing, doors and switches, pick up and throw
    • Detection: finding bodies, peripheral vision, noticing moved objects
    • Temporal Drift: 3+ powers in 10 s → glitches, false ghosts, a 5 s lock
    • Final characters (everyone is a placeholder mannequin), art, lighting, sound

    Prototypes

    Each mechanic was built and recorded in the test lab before it went into a level: aiming, Rewind, Slow (two passes), Fast Forward, Possibility Vision, cover, crouch, detection ranges, the detection system (two passes), enemy AI, takedowns and grabs, and combat.

    Open questions

    • Final names, and a real or fictional city (working: real Bengaluru).
    • Whether Meher and Rehaan's relationship is ever named.
    • Sen's final fate (working: he stays in the branch).
    • Whether guards ever shoot (deferred; the slice has no firearms in combat).
    • Every number in this document is a starting value, to be tuned in play-tests.
